messages:
Maya Patel: morning — big picture proposal: break routing policy into three small services: match -> score -> enforce. goal: safer rollouts, smaller hot paths, easier canaries. tradeoff: extra RPCs and surface area.
Ravi Singh: i'm into the decomposition. key is minimizing data passed from match->score. avoid high-cardinality payloads.
Maya Patel: idea: match returns an ordered list of candidate_route_id (stable uuid) + tiny attrs (region,tier,compat_flags). everything else comes from scorer.
Liam O'Connor: stable ids are non-negotiable. otherwise rollout compatibility is a mess. how do we represent compatibility flags? bitset or enum?
Evelyn Park: prefer a small bitmask with documented bits. easier to validate and low cardinality.
Andre Gomez: tenant overrides are sticky: can't hit tenant DB per request. options: sidecar cache with invalidation, or edge-provided signed override blob read once per session.
Ravi Singh: signed override blob is attractive but we need cheap validation. include a version field + HMAC signature, verify in scorer/sidecar.
Maya Patel: agreed. we should PCI-like trust boundary for edge overrides. default to sidecar cache if signature absent.
Liam O'Connor: scoring should be functional/pure (no side effects) so we can run it in-process for Dedicated deployments. enforcement can be the only side-effecting step and emit audit logs async.
Evelyn Park: makes testing simpler: run scorer deterministically in sim. also helps nightly trace replay.
Andre Gomez: ops concern: two runtimes (in-process native vs sidecar/wasm) may drift. need strong cross-runtime integration tests and scorer version pinning in configs.
Ravi Singh: on policy authoring: current JSON blobs are too ad-hoc. propose a terse DSL that compiles to stable opcodes. then runtimes (native/wasm) can share the same compiled spec.
Liam O'Connor: wasm runtime is great for tenant-supplied logic. cold start costs matter; plan: per-host compiled-module cache with LRU and prewarm hooks.
Evelyn Park: fallback: native scorer if wasm module unavailable or fails to start. explicit degrade mode in the proto.
Maya Patel: scoring outputs should be structured: score numeric, priority_token, cost_estimate, latency_hint, and deterministic enum labels. avoid free-form strings in hot path to prevent cardinality blowups.
Ravi Singh: also require that scorer telemetry emits only pre-approved enum keys; any new key must go through schema change.
Liam O'Connor: admission service should consume cost_estimate + latency_hint to make fast accept/reject decisions without recomputing score.
Evelyn Park: preemption model: scorer hands out priority_tokens. admission consumes tokens under pressure and emits reclaim events. simplifies coupling.
Andre Gomez: compatibility: maintain an opcode compatibility matrix. runtime vN supports opcode set M. old policies either blocked at compile-time or auto-translated with warnings. ops playbook needs explicit rollback steps.
Maya Patel: testing plan: property-based tests for scorer monotonicity/consistency, nightly trace replay in sim, and cross-runtime integration tests. enforce scorer pinning during rollouts.
Ravi Singh: i'll draft the DSL spec + sample policies and contrived edge cases to validate invariants.
Liam O'Connor: i'll prototype wasm bootstrap + module cache + prewarm endpoints.
Evelyn Park: i'll simulate sidecar cache TTLs and invalidation signals; measure p99 for cache miss vs hit.
Andre Gomez: i'll write the ops compatibility matrix and rollback runbook.
ops-bot: Deploybot: created epic "policy-choreography-decomp" (RD-8123) and assigned to Maya. :white_check_mark:
Maya Patel: timeline: can we get a minimal proto + ID scheme draft by next Wednesday? want a short loop to surface infra surprises.
Ravi Singh: yes. i'll also include property tests scaffold.
Liam O'Connor: ping infra once you have the wasm artifact; i'll wire caching.
Evelyn Park: note on metrics: default rollups should be at route/region. tenant-level enums only if explicitly opted-in to avoid cardinality spikes.
Maya Patel: final note: proto must expose explicit fallback modes: "exact" and "best_effort". no implicit silent fallbacks.
Andre Gomez: +1 for explicit.
Maya Patel: thanks all — will post proto link in this thread when ready. :v:
